key_insight: Changing the weight factors used to compute Park’s control temperature can noticeably alter predicted hypersonic nonequilibrium flow behavior, especially for Earth reentry cases.
engineering_relevance: This sensitivity matters for designing and validating hypersonic thermal protection systems because it can shift temperature, species, and heat-flux predictions near the shock and stagnation point.
method: Reactive Navier-Stokes simulations of hypersonic reentry flows
Two-temperature non-equilibrium modeling with Park’s formulation
Earth (11-species) and Mars (8-species) chemistry for FIRE II and Mars Pathfinder capsules
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparisons of Mach number, temperature modes, mass fractions, and stagnation-point convective heat flux along the stagnation streamline, showing strong sensitivity for FIRE II but little change for Mars Pathfinder.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on the chosen weight-factor set and may not generalize across all reentry conditions or chemistry models without further validation.
paper_title: Influence of Park's Two-Temperature Model Control Temperature on the Flow Properties in Hypersonic Reentry Conditions
